world.title: Israeli election pits Netanyahu against Eisenkot with coalition uncertain
world.summary: Israelis vote on Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the first parliamentary election since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeking to remain in office and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, head of the Yashar party, leading the principal challenge. Polls indicate that neither Netanyahu’
world.content: Israelis vote on Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the first parliamentary election since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeking to remain in office and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, head of the Yashar party, leading the principal challenge. Polls indicate that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition is likely to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset, leaving smaller parties potentially decisive. The campaign has focused on Netanyahu’s responsibility for the security failures before the 2023 attack, Israel’s handling of the wars that followed, and exemptions from military service for many ultra-Orthodox men. Netanyahu has emphasized security threats, including Iran, while Eisenkot has called for a change in leadership and greater accountability. Voters choose party lists, not a prime minister directly; coalition negotiations after the count will determine who can command parliamentary support. The contest could lead to lengthy negotiations, and official results are scheduled for publication on Nov. 4.

world.title: Ukraine says satellite network limits ruled out Musk’s drone-strike claim
world.summary: Ukrainian officials rejected SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk’s claim that Ukraine’s military used the commercial Starlink satellite network for offensive drone strikes, saying existing service restrictions made the operations he described impossible. The dispute follows last week’s disruption of Starshield, SpaceX’s m
world.content: Ukrainian officials rejected SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk’s claim that Ukraine’s military used the commercial Starlink satellite network for offensive drone strikes, saying existing service restrictions made the operations he described impossible. The dispute follows last week’s disruption of Starshield, SpaceX’s military-focused service, which Ukraine said interfered with drone operations. Service returned to normal speeds on Saturday. Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense technology adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said commercial Starlink terminals in Ukraine were limited to 70–90 kilometers per hour and did not work in Russia, preventing their use for medium- or long-range strikes. Musk said Ukraine had breached the service’s terms and that SpaceX had closed the loophole. He has maintained that the U.S. government controls Starshield. Responsibility for ordering the Starshield restrictions remained disputed after service was restored. Musk has attributed control to the U.S. government, while President Donald Trump has denied ordering the changes. Separately, the Associated Press reported that Russia agreed to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month.
world.image_alt: Ukraine says satellite network limits ruled out Musk’s drone-strike claim

world.title: China’s Communist Party opens discipline talks before Xi’s 2027 term bid
world.summary: China’s Communist Party opened a four-day Central Committee meeting in Beijing on Monday. President Xi Jinping presented a draft plan to tighten party discipline, curb corruption and ensure officials carry out central directives. The closed-door fifth plenum is scheduled to end Thursday, when a summary of its decisions
world.content: China’s Communist Party opened a four-day Central Committee meeting in Beijing on Monday. President Xi Jinping presented a draft plan to tighten party discipline, curb corruption and ensure officials carry out central directives. The closed-door fifth plenum is scheduled to end Thursday, when a summary of its decisions is expected. The party congress is scheduled for 2027, when Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term as party leader and senior posts will be reshuffled. Analysts say the meeting gives Xi an opportunity to reinforce loyalty and compliance with policy, while recent purges have left leadership positions vacant and attendance unusually low. The committee may confirm removals and consider appointments to the Central Military Commission, the party’s top military body, though Xi could defer changes until next year’s congress. China is also contending with weak domestic spending, a prolonged property-sector crisis and strained ties with the United States.
world.image_alt: China’s Communist Party opens discipline talks before Xi’s 2027 term bid

world.title: Trump renews Netanyahu endorsement before Israel vote, urges Iran campaign
world.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed his public endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, urging Israelis to re-elect him in the Oct. 27 parliamentary election and saying they must “finish the job” against Iran. The appeal came a week after Trump’s first endorsement. Reports cited by The Times
world.content: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed his public endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, urging Israelis to re-elect him in the Oct. 27 parliamentary election and saying they must “finish the job” against Iran. The appeal came a week after Trump’s first endorsement. Reports cited by The Times of Israel and News18 said Netanyahu had sought another public show of support as polls indicated his governing coalition was far short of a majority. Trump credited their partnership with U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran and claimed the country had lost its navy and air force and faced 301% inflation. Israel and the United States launched the war on Feb. 28, according to The Times of Israel. Netanyahu’s opponents said Israelis, not a foreign leader, would choose their government.
world.image_alt: Trump renews Netanyahu endorsement before Israel vote, urges Iran campaign

world.title: Netanyahu warns Iran against disrupting Israel
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Iran and its allied groups that any attack intended to disrupt Israel’s Oct. 27 parliamentary election would draw a “disproportionate” response. He said intelligence indicated a possible threat and the military was ready for defensive and offensive action. He did not ide
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Iran and its allied groups that any attack intended to disrupt Israel’s Oct. 27 parliamentary election would draw a “disproportionate” response. He said intelligence indicated a possible threat and the military was ready for defensive and offensive action. He did not identify a specific planned attack. Israel is due to elect all 120 members of the Knesset, and the vote could end Netanyahu’s long tenure. Israeli television also reported a dispute between Netanyahu and military chief Eyal Zamir over an Iran-related directive. The report said Zamir sought a detailed discussion and legal guarantees before carrying it out; Netanyahu called the account “nothing but rubbish.” Opposition leader Yair Lapid accused Netanyahu of seeking escalation to delay the vote, while challenger Gadi Eisenkot accused him of using the Iran threat for political purposes. The U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran began in February. An April ceasefire halted sustained bombardment, though disagreements over shipping access and a blockade remain. U.S. President Donald Trump has raised both a new attack and a deal as options; Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said further strikes would not change Tehran’s policies.
world.image_alt: Netanyahu warns Iran against disrupting Israel

world.title: Storms kill two in Britain, cut power and disrupt northern Europe
world.summary: Storms Austen and Boelo killed two men in Britain and left more than 150,000 homes without electricity across northern Europe on Sunday, while hundreds of flights were cancelled or diverted. A 60-year-old man died in southwestern Scotland and a man in his 20s was killed in north London, the Guardian reported; falling t
world.content: Storms Austen and Boelo killed two men in Britain and left more than 150,000 homes without electricity across northern Europe on Sunday, while hundreds of flights were cancelled or diverted. A 60-year-old man died in southwestern Scotland and a man in his 20s was killed in north London, the Guardian reported; falling trees and wind-blown scaffolding also injured people in France, Germany and Belgium. The storms struck about 24 hours apart. Britain’s Energy Networks Association said more than 400,000 homes had lost power at some point, while France’s Enedis reported 59,000 still without electricity at midday Sunday after a peak of about 288,000. Winds reached 135 kph in western Scotland, where fallen trees and power lines blocked roads and railways; flights, ferries and trains were also disrupted across the region. Authorities warned of flooding and further disruption into Monday. Scotland’s government said another low-pressure system could bring more wet and windy weather early in the week, while travel operators and officials urged people to check service updates before setting out.
world.image_alt: Storms kill two in Britain, cut power and disrupt northern Europe

world.title: Trump invokes 9/11 to attack Muslim Senate candidate in Michigan
world.summary: President Donald Trump used a Michigan campaign rally on Sunday to portray Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as a security threat, calling him a “jihadist” and likening efforts to stop his election to the resistance of passengers who fought hijackers on Sept. 11, 2001. There is no evidence El-Sayed belongs to
world.content: President Donald Trump used a Michigan campaign rally on Sunday to portray Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as a security threat, calling him a “jihadist” and likening efforts to stop his election to the resistance of passengers who fought hijackers on Sept. 11, 2001. There is no evidence El-Sayed belongs to the Muslim Brotherhood, and the Michigan-born candidate has denied any ties to extremist groups. El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, is running against Republican Mike Rogers for the Senate seat being vacated by retiring Democrat Gary Peters. The Nov. 3 contest could affect control of the Senate. Rogers has alleged links between El-Sayed and the Muslim Brotherhood but told NBC he had never called him a terrorist. El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty “shameful”. Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, condemned the president’s remarks, while El-Sayed’s campaign said the candidate would focus on lowering costs. At the same Port Huron rally, Trump predicted a U.S.-Canada trade agreement would come “pretty soon” but offered no terms or negotiating timeline. The trade talks broke down in August, prompting tariffs on about $20 billion in goods and Canadian retaliation.

world.title: Marine Le Pen launches 2027 presidential bid amid French unrest
world.summary: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and a frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race, formally launched her campaign at a rally in Orléans on Oct. 25, promising to restore public order and national confidence. Her launch followed a day of nationwide demonstrations against the cost of li
world.content: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and a frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race, formally launched her campaign at a rally in Orléans on Oct. 25, promising to restore public order and national confidence. Her launch followed a day of nationwide demonstrations against the cost of living, when more than 400,000 people marched and police made more than 1,300 arrests after clashes broke out. Le Pen accused President Emmanuel Macron’s centrist government of lacking authority and made security and immigration central to her campaign, pledging tougher border controls, the expulsion of foreign offenders and “zero tolerance” policing. Unions and Yellow Vest protesters have said they will continue demonstrations in the weeks ahead. The presidential vote is expected in April 2027, with a runoff in May if no candidate wins a majority. Le Pen is appealing a conviction for embezzling European Parliament funds. The National Rally congress also re-elected Jordan Bardella as party president and presented him as her choice for prime minister if she wins.
world.image_alt: Marine Le Pen launches 2027 presidential bid amid French unrest

business.title: Bitcoin falls below $80,000 as traders brace for Fed decision
business.summary: Bitcoin fell nearly 2% to about $79,800 on Monday as investors reduced risk before the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 28 rate decision. Ether and XRP also declined. Traders are watching for signals from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh about a possible December rate increase, which could tighten liquidity. Selling in technology shares an
business.content: Bitcoin fell nearly 2% to about $79,800 on Monday as investors reduced risk before the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 28 rate decision. Ether and XRP also declined. Traders are watching for signals from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh about a possible December rate increase, which could tighten liquidity. Selling in technology shares and outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds added pressure. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $773.5 million in withdrawals on Oct. 22 and 23, though net inflows over five days totaled about $301.2 million. The week also brings the Fed decision, a U.S. inflation report on Oct. 29 and the expiry of an estimated $11 billion in Bitcoin options on Oct. 30.
business.image_alt: Bitcoin falls below $80,000 as traders brace for Fed decision

business.summary: The Trump administration removed 50% tariffs on 22 categories of Canadian goods and added 100 categories, exempting about $2.5 billion in imports and newly targeting roughly $2.6 billion. Tariffs on packaging products had hurt Maine apple and blueberry growers. At a Sunday rally in Port Huron, Michigan, President Donal
business.content: The Trump administration removed 50% tariffs on 22 categories of Canadian goods and added 100 categories, exempting about $2.5 billion in imports and newly targeting roughly $2.6 billion. Tariffs on packaging products had hurt Maine apple and blueberry growers. At a Sunday rally in Port Huron, Michigan, President Donald Trump said a U.S.-Canada trade deal could come “pretty soon,” but offered no terms or timeline. White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said talks were gaining momentum, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had been speaking with Canadian officials. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The move required interim financing. In the United States, one couple is considering selling a $1.5 million family home and buying a $600,000 property to
business.content: Hans and Renate Wymann set a goal of selling their house by age 75. After a five-year search, they chose to buy an apartment rather than rent because rents were high. The move required interim financing. In the United States, one couple is considering selling a $1.5 million family home and buying a $600,000 property to invest the difference, but one spouse says she cannot bear to leave the home where they raised their children. Financial advisers cited by GoBankingRates warn that buying a home in retirement can tie up savings and add insurance, tax and maintenance costs for people on fixed incomes.

business.title: US data center opposition puts AI infrastructure plans before voters
business.summary: Opposition to data center construction has become an election issue in the United States, where 16 states have proposed laws to block or temporarily halt new facilities. In Los Angeles County, Alhambra voters will decide Nov. 3 whether to make the city’s existing data center ban permanent; Monterey Park voters approved
business.content: Opposition to data center construction has become an election issue in the United States, where 16 states have proposed laws to block or temporarily halt new facilities. In Los Angeles County, Alhambra voters will decide Nov. 3 whether to make the city’s existing data center ban permanent; Monterey Park voters approved a citywide ban in June. Critics cite electricity demand, water use, pollution and pressure on local infrastructure. Supporters argue data centers bring investment, tax revenue, jobs and capacity needed for AI and national security. Technology companies are expected to spend $765 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, with spending projected to exceed $1 trillion next year.
business.image_alt: US data center opposition puts AI infrastructure plans before voters

business.title: Apollo says AI spending has yet to lift profits beyond tech
business.summary: An analysis published Saturday by Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Slok found no measurable financial payoff from artificial intelligence for U.S. companies outside the technology sector. The analysis compares the “S&P 493” — the S&P 500 excluding Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tes
business.content: An analysis published Saturday by Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Slok found no measurable financial payoff from artificial intelligence for U.S. companies outside the technology sector. The analysis compares the “S&P 493” — the S&P 500 excluding Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — with those seven large technology companies. Since 2022, technology firms’ revenue per employee rose from about $550,000 to nearly $800,000, while the figure for the rest of the S&P 500 remained near $550,000. Profit margins outside tech have stayed around 10%, and Slok found no clear productivity gain. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are due to report earnings this week. Slok questioned whether businesses can turn cheaper AI models into higher revenue and margins, while Apollo’s analysis said some companies are beginning to view AI spending as a cost that weighs on margins.
business.image_alt: Apollo says AI spending has yet to lift profits beyond tech

business.title: India
business.summary: India has stabilized its currency, but the rupee weakened as importers made dollar payments and long-dollar positions rose modestly, Reuters reported on Monday. International Monetary Fund official Krishna Srinivasan said the rupee is now more flexible and that the exchange rate should serve as the first line of defens
business.content: India has stabilized its currency, but the rupee weakened as importers made dollar payments and long-dollar positions rose modestly, Reuters reported on Monday. International Monetary Fund official Krishna Srinivasan said the rupee is now more flexible and that the exchange rate should serve as the first line of defense, according to an interview published by The Indian Express.

business.title: Investors reassess AI boom as debt and weak returns raise bubble fears
business.summary: Investors are increasingly questioning whether the artificial intelligence boom can generate enough revenue to support its spending, as AI-linked shares slide and borrowing costs rise. Concerns center on data-center construction and computing investments financed partly with debt, while some early business users are sc
business.content: Investors are increasingly questioning whether the artificial intelligence boom can generate enough revenue to support its spending, as AI-linked shares slide and borrowing costs rise. Concerns center on data-center construction and computing investments financed partly with debt, while some early business users are scaling back after finding that error correction, security work and low-quality output reduce productivity gains. Data-center investment accounted for nearly all U.S. economic growth last winter and spring, and companies tied to AI make up about 70% of the Nasdaq 100’s weight. Investors are also watching whether highly leveraged infrastructure providers can service their debt. Infrastructure provider CoreWeave’s 9.75% bonds yielded nearly 15% on Oct. 14, while its shares fell more than 15% that day. Strategists disagree on whether the pullback is nearing an end. Anthropic plans an initial public offering next month, followed by OpenAI next year.
business.image_alt: Investors reassess AI boom as debt and weak returns raise bubble fears

business.title: Musk says SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt for AI chips
business.summary: SpaceX Chief Executive Elon Musk said Sunday the company had closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy graphics processing units for artificial-intelligence systems, with deliveries expected in the first half of 2027. Bloomberg reported that pricing discussions were still ongoing, leaving it unclear whether all deal
business.content: SpaceX Chief Executive Elon Musk said Sunday the company had closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy graphics processing units for artificial-intelligence systems, with deliveries expected in the first half of 2027. Bloomberg reported that pricing discussions were still ongoing, leaving it unclear whether all deal terms had been finalized. Musk attributed SpaceX’s access to financing to its investment-grade credit rating and revenue from Starlink satellite internet and rocket launches. In the third quarter, SpaceX reported $14.58 billion in revenue, including $7.56 billion from its AI business. Capital spending reached $19.6 billion, and Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen forecast $35 billion to $40 billion in fourth-quarter spending. Musk also warned that more than 200 AI-focused cloud providers, known as neoclouds, could face consolidation or failure as lenders become more selective.
business.image_alt: Musk says SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt for AI chips

science.title: Underground carbon storage reached record 43.6 million tons in 2024
science.summary: Global geological carbon storage reached a record 43.6 million metric tons in 2024, according to the London Register of Subsurface CO₂ Storage’s 2026 annual report, which tracks 70 projects in 17 countries. The report says cumulative storage over three decades reached 421.7 million metric tons. The report’s director, I
science.content: Global geological carbon storage reached a record 43.6 million metric tons in 2024, according to the London Register of Subsurface CO₂ Storage’s 2026 annual report, which tracks 70 projects in 17 countries. The report says cumulative storage over three decades reached 421.7 million metric tons. The report’s director, Imperial College London professor Samuel Krevor, said reported annual storage more than doubled from 2016 to 2024. He said storage would need to reach at least 1 billion metric tons a year by 2050 to meet the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C target. The report also revised earlier totals after identifying accounting issues and warned that incomplete 2025 project data should not be treated as a full-year global figure.
science.image_alt: Underground carbon storage reached record 43.6 million tons in 2024

science.title: Nobel physicist Claude Cohen-Tannoudji dies at 93 after pioneering laser cooling
science.summary: French physicist Claude Cohen-Tannoudji, who shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing methods to cool and trap atoms with laser light, died in Paris on Oct. 22 at age 93, the Kastler Brossel Laboratory confirmed. His work made it possible to cool atoms to temperatures of a few nanokelvins, enabling researc
science.content: French physicist Claude Cohen-Tannoudji, who shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing methods to cool and trap atoms with laser light, died in Paris on Oct. 22 at age 93, the Kastler Brossel Laboratory confirmed. His work made it possible to cool atoms to temperatures of a few nanokelvins, enabling researchers to probe their quantum properties with greater precision. The techniques helped advance atomic clocks and atom interferometers. Cohen-Tannoudji also trained generations of physicists and wrote widely used quantum mechanics textbooks with Bernard Diu and Franck Laloë. His research helped establish laser cooling as a tool in modern atomic physics.
science.image_alt: Nobel physicist Claude Cohen-Tannoudji dies at 93 after pioneering laser cooling

science.title: Rubin Observatory releases Seagull Nebula test image as sky survey begins
science.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has released a test image of the Seagull Nebula, also known as IC 2177, about 3,700 light-years from Earth. The observatory captured the image with its 144-megapixel Commissioning Camera. The nebula’s head is the star-forming cloud Sharpless 2-292; its pink glow comes from hydrogen gas ene
science.content: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has released a test image of the Seagull Nebula, also known as IC 2177, about 3,700 light-years from Earth. The observatory captured the image with its 144-megapixel Commissioning Camera. The nebula’s head is the star-forming cloud Sharpless 2-292; its pink glow comes from hydrogen gas energized by young stars, while surrounding blue hues come from starlight reflected by dust. The image was part of tests of the observatory’s hardware, software and image processing. Rubin has since switched to its 3,200-megapixel main camera, which captures an image every 30 seconds and covers roughly 20 times more sky per frame; its 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time has begun.
science.image_alt: Rubin Observatory releases Seagull Nebula test image as sky survey begins

science.title: Webb identifies three feeding black holes in an ancient galaxy
science.summary: Astronomers led by the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics identified three actively feeding black holes in galaxy J0148-4214, whose light dates from 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang. Two are only 620 light-years apart; a third lies farther out. Separate studies reported that Webb images show Arp 220
science.content: Astronomers led by the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics identified three actively feeding black holes in galaxy J0148-4214, whose light dates from 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang. Two are only 620 light-years apart; a third lies farther out. Separate studies reported that Webb images show Arp 220 is two merging spiral galaxies, while stellar age measurements based on Gaia data support a two-stage formation of the Milky Way’s disk. The black-hole team estimates the two central objects will merge within a few hundred million years.
science.image_alt: Webb identifies three feeding black holes in an ancient galaxy

science.title: October
science.summary: October’s full moon, known as the Hunter’s Moon, reached peak illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT on Oct. 26, with Saturn appearing nearby in the evening sky. The moon looked nearly full on both Oct. 25 and Oct. 26 and rose in the east around sunset in the Northern Hemisphere. Saturn appeared as a steady golden point of lig
science.content: October’s full moon, known as the Hunter’s Moon, reached peak illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT on Oct. 26, with Saturn appearing nearby in the evening sky. The moon looked nearly full on both Oct. 25 and Oct. 26 and rose in the east around sunset in the Northern Hemisphere. Saturn appeared as a steady golden point of light, though the moon’s brightness could make it harder to spot. The name Hunter’s Moon refers to the full moon after the harvest season, when cleared fields and bright moonlight aided hunting, according to historical explanations cited by the Old Farmer’s Almanac. The moon was due to pass close to the Pleiades star cluster on the nights of Oct. 27 and 28.

science.title: NASA plans 2027 lunar docking tests before 2028 astronaut landing
science.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency remains on track for Artemis III, a two-week mission planned for next summer to test docking between its Orion capsule and lunar landers built by SpaceX and Blue Origin. The crew will orbit Earth rather than travel to the Moon; Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028, is intende
science.content: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency remains on track for Artemis III, a two-week mission planned for next summer to test docking between its Orion capsule and lunar landers built by SpaceX and Blue Origin. The crew will orbit Earth rather than travel to the Moon; Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028, is intended to return astronauts to the lunar surface. The docking tests will require three launches in quick succession. Orion is scheduled to dock first with Blue Origin’s lander, then with SpaceX’s Starship. NASA has not yet chosen which company will provide the Artemis IV lander, and officials say they will keep both options open as long as possible.
science.image_alt: NASA plans 2027 lunar docking tests before 2028 astronaut landing

science.title: UK space cleanup mission poll puts Binface among leading names
science.summary: A reader poll by The Register put “Binface” and “Binny McBinface” among the leading proposed names for the UK’s Active Debris Removal Mission, a planned effort to remove two defunct British satellites from orbit. The suggestions are not described as the UK Space Agency’s official choice. ClearSpace UK is developing the
science.content: A reader poll by The Register put “Binface” and “Binny McBinface” among the leading proposed names for the UK’s Active Debris Removal Mission, a planned effort to remove two defunct British satellites from orbit. The suggestions are not described as the UK Space Agency’s official choice. ClearSpace UK is developing the mission under a contract worth about $81 million. The target launch date for its spacecraft is 2029, from Scotland’s SaxaVord Spaceport, with the two satellites due to be removed by 2032.
science.image_alt: UK space cleanup mission poll puts Binface among leading names

science.title: Global assessment puts 96% of shallow reefs at collapse risk by 2075
science.summary: A global assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) finds that 96% of assessed shallow-water coral reef ecosystems are critically endangered, facing an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075. The assessment covers reef systems in 127 tropical and subtropical marine regions and places all 1
science.content: A global assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) finds that 96% of assessed shallow-water coral reef ecosystems are critically endangered, facing an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075. The assessment covers reef systems in 127 tropical and subtropical marine regions and places all 17 Australian reef ecosystems included in the highest-risk category. Researchers identify climate-driven ocean warming and marine heat waves as the leading threat. Coral reefs provide habitat for about a quarter of marine species and support fisheries, tourism and coastal protection. The IUCN defines collapse as the loss of most reef-building hard corals, which algae, rubble and other organisms then replace. The assessment says reducing greenhouse-gas emissions is crucial, alongside stronger local protection and restoration; pollution and overfishing also add pressure. The IUCN released the report during international biodiversity discussions in Yerevan, Armenia.
science.image_alt: Global assessment puts 96% of shallow reefs at collapse risk by 2075

sports.title: Sunderland end four-game losing run with 0-0 draw against Leeds
sports.summary: Sunderland ended a four-match Premier League losing streak with a 0-0 draw against Leeds at the Stadium of Light on Sunday, October 25, but remained bottom with five points from eight games. Leeds moved to 11 points and seventh place after recording their fifth draw in eight league matches. Storm Boelo brought fierce,
sports.content: Sunderland ended a four-match Premier League losing streak with a 0-0 draw against Leeds at the Stadium of Light on Sunday, October 25, but remained bottom with five points from eight games. Leeds moved to 11 points and seventh place after recording their fifth draw in eight league matches. Storm Boelo brought fierce, shifting winds that disrupted passing and crossing. Sunderland’s returning striker Brian Brobbey twice tested Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford in the first half, while Sunderland winger Nilson Angulo drew further saves after the break. At the other end, Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs denied midfielder Sean Longstaff late on, and Longstaff’s final effort was blocked near the goal line. Sunderland manager Régis Le Bris said his team had shown intensity and togetherness, while Leeds manager Daniel Farke described the point and clean sheet as a worthwhile away result in the conditions. Sunderland’s next league fixture is away to Coventry on Saturday.
sports.image_alt: Sunderland end four-game losing run with 0-0 draw against Leeds

sports.title: Seahawks hand Chiefs first loss; all eight North teams have winning records
sports.summary: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday, handing the defending champions their first loss of the season, while the Minnesota Vikings remained the NFL’s only unbeaten team at 6-0. Week 7 also marked a league first: all eight teams in the AFC and NFC North had winning records, with the Cleveland B
sports.content: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday, handing the defending champions their first loss of the season, while the Minnesota Vikings remained the NFL’s only unbeaten team at 6-0. Week 7 also marked a league first: all eight teams in the AFC and NFC North had winning records, with the Cleveland Browns leading the AFC North and Minnesota topping the NFC North. Other results included the Cincinnati Bengals’ 35-13 comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens, the Atlanta Falcons’ 29-20 win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers, and the Detroit Lions’ 20-17 win over Green Bay. Pittsburgh beat New Orleans 16-10 in the NFL’s first game in France, played at Stade de France in Saint-Denis. Week 7 concludes Monday night, when the Dallas Cowboys are scheduled to visit the Philadelphia Eagles.
sports.image_alt: Seahawks hand Chiefs first loss; all eight North teams have winning records

sports.title: Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy leads 27-21 overtime win over Texans
sports.summary: The New York Giants beat the Houston Texans 27-21 in overtime on Oct. 25, with quarterback J.J. McCarthy winning his first start for New York after joining the team from Minnesota. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards without a turnover, while running back Cam Skattebo rushed for 124 yards and a touchdown.
sports.content: The New York Giants beat the Houston Texans 27-21 in overtime on Oct. 25, with quarterback J.J. McCarthy winning his first start for New York after joining the team from Minnesota. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards without a turnover, while running back Cam Skattebo rushed for 124 yards and a touchdown. Skattebo’s 42-yard run in overtime set up Devin Singletary’s 30-yard game-winning score. Skattebo drew a 15-yard unnecessary-roughness penalty for lowering his helmet into Texans safety M.J. Stewart. Afterward, he said he would not change his running style despite the prospect of further flags or fines. The Giants, now 4-2-1, have a bye before visiting the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 8.

sports.content: Newcastle United beat Crystal Palace 2-0 at Selhurst Park on Oct. 25, with William Osula and Harvey Barnes scoring in the first 13 minutes of the second half. Palace had chances before the break, but Newcastle took control after the restart. A video assistant referee review ruled out a Joe Willock goal for offside. The defeat left Palace 17th with seven points from eight league matches, one point above the relegation zone, and extended their winless run to four games. They have conceded 19 goals, the Premier League’s worst defensive record. A week earlier, they lost 5-0 to Brighton. Palace manager Pierre Sage said his team lost concentration for 15 minutes after halftime and maintained that he could turn results around. Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle called the win deserved after two league defeats. Palace’s next league match is away to Tottenham on Oct. 31, followed by Liverpool on Nov. 8.

sports.content: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said the NFL and its players’ union discussed staging all 16 regular-season games abroad in a single week during the 2020 collective bargaining talks. Each team would receive a second bye. The idea did not advance after owners pursued a 17th game, which the league introduced in 2021. Rodgers backed the idea after Pittsburgh beat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 on Sunday in the NFL’s first regular-season game in France. He said a coordinated week could help grow the sport and urged the league to fund longer visits and community events for teams abroad. The NFL’s 2026 schedule includes a record nine international games. Commissioner Roger Goodell said the league plans to play in Tokyo in 2027 or 2028 and is pursuing as many as 16 overseas games per season. The league’s remaining international stops this season are Madrid, Munich and Mexico City over the coming month.

sports.content: The Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Los Angeles Clippers 108-101 on Sunday, but All-Star forward Jalen Williams left on a stretcher after suffering a serious injury to his lower left leg with 1:14 remaining. Williams landed awkwardly while driving toward the basket after contact from Clippers players Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr.; officials upgraded Dunn’s foul to a flagrant 1 after review. The team had not announced a diagnosis by Monday morning. The defending 2025 NBA champions improved to 3-0. Williams averaged 23.6 points per game in the 2025 Finals, but injuries limited him to five playoff appearances last season. Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said the team expected an update on Monday, Oct. 26. Oklahoma City was scheduled to host the Phoenix Suns that night. Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said the team would have to hold the fort until Williams returned.

sports.content: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 at Lumen Field on Sunday, Oct. 25, handing Kansas City its first loss of the season and ending Seattle’s two-game losing streak. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, while running back Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score. Quarterback Sam Darnold threw for 257 yards and a touchdown as Seattle improved to 4-3; the Chiefs fell to 5-1. Seattle’s defense held Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to 165 passing yards with one interception, limited Kansas City to 213 total yards and kept it out of the red zone. Kenneth Walker III, the former Seattle running back who joined Kansas City in the offseason after winning Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks, gained 36 yards on 14 carries. Seattle moved within two games of the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West after San Francisco lost to Atlanta earlier Sunday to fall to 6-1. Seattle next hosts the Chicago Bears, while Kansas City visits AFC West rival Denver in Week 8.

sports.content: Pakistan secured a place in the one-day international (ODI) tri-series final on Sunday with a one-wicket win over England in Lahore, reaching their target of 242 at 243-9 in 47.1 overs. All-rounder Shadab Khan scored his first ODI century, finishing unbeaten on 113 from 96 balls, and shared an unbroken 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf, who scored seven not out. The partnership was the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI chase. England reduced Pakistan to 154-9 but could not take the final wicket. Earlier, Ben Duckett’s 105 helped England reach 241 all out; Sam Curran added 42 in a 93-run partnership with Duckett. Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi took four wickets for 46 runs, while England seamer Jamie Overton claimed three for 43. The defeat was England’s third in as many tri-series matches, leaving their chances of reaching the final dependent on the remaining results. Pakistan face Sri Lanka on Tuesday, October 27; Sri Lanka then play England on October 29. The final is scheduled for October 31 in Lahore.
